newsitem.title: USA: KCP&L pulls plug on UtiliCorp merger.
newsitem.headline: KCP&L pulls plug on UtiliCorp merger.

text.p: Kansas City Power & Light Co. said Wednesday it abandoned its eight-month effort to merge with UtiliCorp United Inc.
Kansas City Power cited a lack of shareholder support in the face of a more lucrative, though hostile, offer from Western Resources Inc.
On Tuesday, Western announced what it called the final vote count, which showed about 38 percent of KCP&L's 61.9 million total shares outstanding backed the UtiliCorp deal.
In a statement, KCP&L said the $1.7 billion deal was called off "in view of the failure of KCPL stockholders to approve the KCPL/UtiliCorp merger."
Western's bid, repeatedly rebuffed by KCP&L management despite richer per-share terms and a larger indicated dividend, is valued at about $1.9 billion.

The outcome of the two-on-one fight against Western has been closely watched by utility officers, directors and investment bankers who have agreed that deregulation of the U.S. electricity will mean more hostile combinations in the future.

A source close to KCP&L said Western now needed 90 percent of KCP&L shares tendered to complete the hostile deal, but a Western spokeswoman said the 90 percent was necessary only for a "short-form" merger, and added that if Western garners a majority of KCP&L shares in the ongoing tender offer, it will, if necessary, install a sympathetic board of directors.
"It leaves only our offer on the table," the Western spokeswoman said.
Meanwhile, the KCP&L source said the company was reviewing its options regarding Western, and declined to comment further.
Under terms of the exchange offer, which expires Oct. 25, KCP&L shareholders can swap each of their shares for $31 worth of Western stock.
On Wednesday, Western stock slipped 12.5 cents to $28.875, KCP&L ended up 25 cents at $27.25 and UtiliCorp fell 25 cents to $27.875, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
Since KCP&L and UtiliCorp announced the ill-fated combination Jan. 22, KCP&L stock has risen almost 2 percent, while Western has fallen almost 16 percent and UtiliCorp about 3.5 percent.
On Aug. 16, KCP&L shareholders voted on the UtiliCorp merger, two days after UtiliCorp's shareholders approved the agreement by a wide margin.
On the day of the KCP&L vote, KCP&L Chairman Drue Jennings said that in the event the friendly combination with UtiliCorp failed to happen, the company would not be for sale.
He was not immediately available for comment.
